Before you start, note these restrictions from the cited documentation:
> User can update the form and hit "Provision EnvironmentService Pod" button. | Source vs Current Comparison section will show difference for only following fields: * Start with [doc-0091]

Documented guidance:
- Users can only copy a provisioning submission if the release version is not end-of-life. [doc-0091]
- If the source provisioning job uses an EOL release set, the Copy Provisioning Job dialog displays an error stating it is not eligible for copying. [doc-0091]
- The system blocks the copy action for EOL release sets at the validation step before the form can be reviewed or edited. [doc-0091]

Sources:

Links, commands, and configurations in this adapted documentation are illustrative.
result.evidence_reason: All supporting quotes match retrieved source passages. The draft correctly answers 'No' to the user's question about bypassing the restriction. The evidence explicitly states that if a source provisioning job uses an EOL release set, the system displays an error message ('not eligible for copying') instead of opening the form for editing. Therefore, the claim that the system blocks the action before the form can be reviewed or edited is supported by the 'Show error message' step in Use Case 2, confirming that editing is impossible in this scenario.

draft.reason: The documentation explicitly states that provisioning submissions with an end-of-life (EOL) release version are not eligible for copying. The system prevents this action by displaying an error message rather than allowing the form to be edited or submitted.

retrieved_sources.text:
Redcontent moved to DocumentationPortal <https://docs.example.com/reference/resource-670>

Scope
-----

Enable users to copy a provisioning submission to simplify the preflight submission process and minimize repetitive work.

Users can copy any provisioning submission if the following conditions are met:

* The submission is associated with the user’s LOBs.
* The release version is not end-of-life.

Use Case Definition
-------------------

The action menu will be available in the following scenarios:

* On the **Preflight Dashboard**:

	+ For all rows where the Type is **ENVIRONMENTSERVICE_PROVISIONING** and the LOB belongs to the user's LOBs.
* On **All PODs**:

	+ For all rows where the LOB belongs to the user's LOBs.
		- The action will use the provisioning record associated with the selected pod as the source record.
* On the **Family Pod Dashboard**:

	+ For all rows where the LOB belongs to the user's LOBs.
		- The action will use the provisioning record associated with the selected pod as the source record.

All fields on the provisioning page are automatically populated from the source record.

Additionally, all fields on the provisioning UI remain editable, allowing users to make any necessary changes after reviewing the information.

retrieved_sources.title: PipelineHub Preflight - Provisioning
retrieved_sources.text:
1. Set the Free Form tag at provisioning time. This will set the Free Form tag on your pod
2. Set the Free Form tag at upgrade time. This will set the Free form tag on your pod

If you realize that you need a Free Form tag applied to your pod outside of provisioning, or upgrade, please file Jira to review.

#### Freeform tag USE_X86_ONLY to honor Middleware14c Pod provisioning /Release set creation

When we need to use a Releaseset flag , in the additional config params on the Provisioning job use the key with format "RS-key1=value1", for eg if you need to set USER_X86_ONLY=true at the release set level , then pass "RS-USER_X86_ONLY=true" in the additional config params and it would set the release set level free form tags, and you can also pass the provisioning level flags along side with it for eg., let say you are passing RS-key1=value1;podKey1=value1;podKey2=value2;RS-key2=value2 to the additional config param then Key1, and Ke2 will be set at release set level as they are prepended by RS- and the other 2 freeform tags podKey1 and podKey2 will be set at the pod level.
